title: S2's runner changes, the rule for which cells count, and the nine discarded cells are published
why: EXP 020's S2 runner (the change-feed scenario) was changed four times, and given a rule for which counted cells are kept, after this record was published and after S2's first counted cells ran. None of it was published on this site. The record says a change is a dated amendment, published first. These were not published first: they were applied by the runner and recorded in its private protocol. This amendment publishes them before S2's report, so the report is judged against rules a reader can see. The lab owns the gap. The runner's owner classified each change, at our request, as changing a measure, which cells count, the verdict rule, or only how a frozen rule is carried out; their answers are recorded below, with the changes that move the primary metric marked as such.
timing: Recorded in the runner's protocol (sha256 c50a7d30..., one private commit c38e3cf1, 2026-10-25 05:38:26Z) after EXP 020 was published (odin-rnd #76, merge 0af2c486) and after S2's first two counted cells (2026-10-25 05:21-05:52 local), which ran on the old code and are discarded. The first kept counted cell started at 06:42:09 local, after that commit. Authored on 2026-10-25, while S2 is still running and before any S2 result is reported. S1, S3 and S4 are not affected.

changes.what: The pgoutput cursor is the commit LSN
changes.class: runner mechanics: a runner bug that lost 1 event; the gate is unchanged
changes.rule: The cursor is the transaction's commit LSN (the Begin message's final_lsn), and a source transaction is applied whole.

changes.class: runner mechanics by the letter (effect and cursor stay in one transaction), but it moves the primary metric by orders of magnitude, so it is treated as a change to the measure
changes.rule: Each consumer applies up to 100 available events in one transaction, with the cursor at the batch end. Before it, at 10x every arm fell behind: lag p50 0.75-4.7 s per event-transaction (the runner owner's figures from smoke cells and the discarded counted cells, not counted measurements).

changes.what: The producer's schedule starts after its payloads and connections exist
changes.class: runner mechanics: a harness timing bug that restores the pre-registered rate; it also moves the measure, MongoDB's most
changes.rule: Seeded random payloads are built, and the writers created, before t0. Before it, every event started late (start-late p95 1.3-38 s in the runner owner's smoke and discarded cells, not counted measurements).

changes.what: The MongoDB consumer applies once its locally buffered changes are exhausted
changes.class: runner mechanics for one arm only; by the runner owner's smoke cells (not counted measurements) it moves MongoDB's 1x lag from p50 2.5 s to about 5 ms, in MongoDB's favour, so it is published as a change to the measure
changes.rule: Apply when the cursor's local buffer is empty (PyMongo 4.10.1's private CommandCursor._data, pinned), the rule pgoutput already followed (an idle stream).

changes.what: The disturbance rule decides which counted cells count
changes.class: changes which cells count; not in the pre-registration
changes.rule: A counted cell that overlapped other heavy work on the host (a browser end-to-end run, filming, another benchmark) is discarded and re-run; a PAUSE file holds the plan between cells. Light single-core unit tests with no browser and no database are judged not heavy, and those cells are kept; that judgement is listed so a reader can disagree.
A lock file refuses a second cell on the stack.

discardedCells.rerun: A second plan pass re-measures every missing cell under the same rules. Nothing is pooled.
discardedCells.disclosed: Five of the nine (the 13:07-14:18 window) were first kept, and the log records them as discarded only when the runner's owner answered our question, at about 21:35 local on 2026-10-25. Interim seed-1 numbers posted earlier, privately, included two of them; the report is computed from the kept cells only.

unchanged: The question, arms, scenarios, gates, primary metrics, margins, component checklist, verdicts, predictions and out-of-scope list of the pre-registration are unchanged, and the frozen record stays byte-identical. Every change above is to how S2's runner carries out the frozen design and which of its cells count.
limits: These changes were made, and run under, before they were published here, so they were not pre-registered in the strict sense: a reader has the runner owner's account of when each was made, with the commit time, not an earlier public record.
Amendments 02 and 04 move the primary metric a long way, and 04 applies to one arm only, in its favour. The S2 report should be read with them in mind.
Whether a disturbance was heavy is the runner owner's judgement, written in the log for each row; the light rows that were kept are not listed cell by cell here.

The protocol pairs MongoDB, per repetition, with the better passing PostgreSQL variant of that repetition. The pre-registration says 'the other store's best variant'. EXP 021's reviewers rejected a per-repetition best for EXP 021 (it is a best-of-two that tilts toward PostgreSQL). This amendment records the protocol as written and does not decide S2's pairing; any change to it is a further dated amendment, published before S2's report.
notBefore: S2's report is published only after this amendment is merged to main of odin-labs-ai/odin-rnd.
